ratings_why.fun: Hold or run is a real choice every turn, and watching the shelf age into Grisel's copies or launder into a growing crew is satisfying; the zone plus seal adds some screen load.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: no tribe today plays inside the shop itself, and a shelf of any tribe's units that both halves read, replays When played effects and fields copies in a fight is new.

verdict_why: v2 cleared the unclear wording; what is left are presentation ideas, and more passes would make it different rather than better.

points.text: Grisel's copies get Wenna's and Nan's buff only if those sit after her in reading order, a hidden rule. Letting Grisel summon before other Start of Combat effects would remove the trap.
Tide-Waiter Hern and Officer Nyx Seize every turn; on a full shelf that pushes out a unit you were holding. Saying "you may Seize" would let a holder keep their stock.
The Auctioneer and Grisel read shelf age, and Nan reads a game-long buy-back count. Show the shelf in oldest-first order and Nan's count on the card so they read at a glance.
Corporal Rufa's "twice" leaves open what the second hit does if the first kills; saying it hits the new unit across, or nothing, would settle it.
Tibby Slick's redirect is invisible on the card's board; it needs a clear slip-past animation, or players won't see why the attacker's neighbour took the hit.

standouts.why: Chief Collector Grisel turns the seized shelf into an army of copies in your empty slots: the customs house becoming the heron's own force reads at once.
Honest Ned, Informer turning in your own unit to buy it back and replay it is the smuggling joke as a mechanic, and simple to read.
The Stoker of the Confiscation Fire is plain to read and in theme: burn seized goods, your biggest unit grows.

weakest.why: Tibby Slick's dodge often does nothing and is hard to see happen.
Narrows Sentry is a generic count-and-grow body with little heron in it.
Nan Silverholt's army buff off a hidden game counter is the least woodland-flavored capstone.

flags.note: Grisel's Contraband copies stacking with Wenna and Nan can climb high, and the payoff depends on a placement order players may miss.
Old Dunmore with Honest Ned and Sergeant Squacco can launder and replay several times a turn; bounded by gold, worth the owner's eye.
